utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Registrar, may I ask you, please, to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-00-39-A, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Before asking for the appearances, as we have a new Defence counsel today, may I introduce myself, Judge Schomburg, acting as Pre-Appeal Judge in this case. The appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, my name is Christine Dahl and with me is Matteo Costi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Can I ask Mr. Krajisnik, can you follow the hearing in a language you understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I thank you. In order to avoid overlaps, I have a very short draft agenda for today. Of course first we have to discuss potential health issues, the detention conditions, the question of counsel, the filing of notice of appeal, pending motions, and of course then it's for the parties to raise other issues if they so want. Let us turn to the first point and this would be, Mr. Krajisnik, do you have any health problems or do you have any complaints you want to raise about the conditions in the United Nations detention facilities? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] No, nothing of significance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I thank you. As regards now the question of counsel. By the decision of last Friday, the Registrar, following an order of the at that time Pre-Appeal Judge and at the same time Presiding Judge in the case, President Pocar, Mr. Colin Nicholls, Queen's counsel, was assigned as Defence counsel. May I ask you to keep the record straight. Do you face any problems in conducting this Defence on appeal in the concrete case, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Is that right? Your Honour, I do face certain problems. As Your Honour knows, I was instructed in this matter or assigned to this matter on Friday afternoon late. Over the weekend, I have actually skim-read the judgement. I have seen Mr. Krajisnik today for about an hour. He has indicated to me that he wishes Mr. Dershowitz from the United States to act as his lead counsel and he has said that if Mr. Dershowitz is not able to act for him or is not allowed to act for him then he wishes to conduct his own Defence. In other words, he does not wish me to represent him. There are two letters I have been handed. One is a letter to Mr. Menon of the Registry from Mr. Dershowitz himself and it's dated the 8th of December. I don't know if Your Honours had a copy of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I hand it up to you. I've only got the one copy. There is a second document which is again a letter to Mr. Menon dated the 9th of December, and that is from a person who was concerned in the Obrenovic case. Perhaps I can hand the documents to Your Honour first and perhaps give some explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I apologise in the direction of the Prosecution. Of course in due course as soon as possible you will get copies of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry that I just did not have another copy and I've only just received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in short, what Mr. Dershowitz is saying is that he wishes to represent Mr. Krajisnik, but he wishes his brother to act as his co-counsel. The second document is a letter from a person who was concerned in the Obrenovic case with which Your Honour no doubt is familiar, where the defendant's brother was proposed as an investigator in the case. It was originally opposed on the basis that it would involve a breach of Rule 16(F) of the Directive, but in due course the brother as investigator was allowed. If that is so, then the accused says in this case the brother of Mr. Dershowitz acting as co-counsel should be acceptable to the Court on the principal as finally resolved in Obrenovic. That in short is the point he wishes to make. Your Honour will have noticed in the letter from Mr. Dershowitz he says that he was not able to appear today because he has health problems, but that he had wanted to be able to appear and to appear for those grounds that I've just put forward. May I make absolutely clear, any question of representation of this accused I would normally not say anything at all because it's really a matter for him and the Court, but he has asked me this afternoon that I should place this position before Your Honour and his application is in short that Mr. Dershowitz should be allowed to represent him and should be assigned in the case with the brother as co-counsel. And he's saying if that is not allowed then he wishes to represent himself. The next matter on Your Honour's agenda is, in fact, the notice of appeal, and I don't wish to stray into that area unduly, but I have of course indicated to the accused that as I am assigned to him as his counsel at this moment in time with a time-limit of 30 days from the date of my assignment, I have absolutely no way of knowing whether I can comply with the Court's orders. And indeed what Mr. Krajisnik has said to me is that I must not do what I cannot do, which is a basic principle so far as advocates are concerned. And with his knowledge of the case he said to me there is no theoretical possibility that I could do a credible job in the time. Your Honour, may I just state the position. As I say, I am rather straying but I think it's appropriate that I should. I've indicated when I was assigned to the case and I've indicated that over the weekend I have read, skim-read, the judgement. At this moment, I have no team, and if the 30-day rule is to apply, the notice of appeal would have to be in by the 7th of January. It puts me in an impossible position, and if I am to have a team it is absolutely essential, even if Your Honour extends the time, it is essential that I should have counsel who preferably was previously involved in the case, not Mr. Stewart, or at least someone who has some knowledge of the case who could give me the assistance that I would desperately need in conducting an appeal. Your Honour, there's the judgement, there's the motions, there's so much of the evidence as may be needed to be read in due course. I have absolutely no idea how long all that will take. I don't make my application for the extension of time at this moment. Your Honour would obviously wish to deal with the point of representation first. May I just add this that I have just summarised what the accused wishes to say, but he has asked me to indicate to Your Honour that he does wish to say something himself. I would ask Your Honour to allow him insofar as it's permissible to say something himself. As I say, I have merely summarised the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm extremely grateful for this summary. And this is an international tribunal, a hybrid tribunal, having both approaches from civil law and common law. I see no obstacle at all to allow Mr. Krajisnik the floor if he so wants to address the Bench, please, Mr. Krajisnik. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to say a few words, and what I would like to say is that if there is any problem I would really like to receive assistance in appointment of Mr. Dershowitz. If there are no problems in that regard I wouldn't want to even spend your time on this. I could, if necessary, give you a history of this case and to tell you what are the efforts that we have taken so far to find out a solution in full cooperation with the Registry. And now that the Dershowitz problem has been solved I would like to ask you once again to approve this appointment. If you need any additional information, I am here and I can give you any additional information necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krajisnik, it's true, only might be some document is missing, it's correct that Trial Chamber I rendered its judgement in this case on 27th September 2006, and immediately afterwards there were two related requests to extend the deadline for filing against appeal against the judgement, both filed by you in person on 6th -- 17 October 2006; that's correct. Under the Rules, the notice of appeal would be due no later than 27th October 2006; however, as the President in this case ruled that there is under Rule 127(B) an opportunity that a Pre-Appeal Judge may on good cause being shown by motion, by motion I emphasise, enlarge or reduce any time-period prescribed by or under the Rules. And it was therefore that another 30 days were already allotted to you, 30 days starting immediately after the assignment of counsel to you. Of course, it's settled jurisprudence when due to lack of time and good cause has been shown, it is always possible to show in greater details the grounds of appeal and/or to add additional grounds of appeal. However, the case has to proceed. It's in -- not only in your own interest that -- because the notice, the term of fair trial no doubt includes that a case be heard as soon as possible and as soon as practicable and that all others waiting for judgement, they are also entitled to have a case heard as soon as possible. I wonder, what was the reason why it was not possible to come to an agreement with Mr. Dershowitz earlier? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm going to try to describe all the efforts that we have made in order to secure a lawyer for me. I really wanted to have a lawyer as soon as possible, a lawyer that is going to handle my appeals. Even before the Trial Chamber judgement was issued, I have contacted certain lawyers. I was thinking if it would not be necessary for me to lodge an appeal, then the Prosecutor is certainly going to lodge an appeal so that the whole process is going to start as soon as possible because I was aware of the 30-day deadline. Immediately after the judgement was pronounced I have obtained approval from lawyer Mr. Brasic and three professors of law from Belgrade, who all stated that they are willing to start to work on my appeals at once. Within seven days I received the reply from the Registry saying that Mr. Brasic is not listed under Rule 46, or was it 45. I asked Mr. Brasic to register on that list, and when he registered on the list it turned out that the Registry has a ban on Mr. Brasic practising law before this Tribunal. At the same time, I wanted to appoint Mr. Dershowitz because ever since this trial began I always wanted Mr. Dershowitz to be part of my team. And Mr. Dershowitz kept replying that he needs far great facilities in order for him to lodge the proper appeal. To in order to appease the Registry I suggested a lawyer who is on the list, Rule 45 list, and I proposed Mr. Dershowitz. A representative of the Registry then contacted both lawyers, and a lawyer who is on the list then gave up and Mr. Dershowitz accepted under certain conditions. He again insisted on certain conditions. After that, I proposed a French lawyer, he agreed to be appointed for my defence; however, he requested additional time in order to do certain checks. And what I have forgotten to say is that immediately after Mr. Brasic fell off the list, the three professors from Belgrade simply gave up as well. So this lawyer from Paris simply said after 15 days that he needs more time to think. I gave his name and his phone number to the representative of the Registry. In the meantime, it looked that Mr. Dershowitz is going to have all his problems solved, and, Your Honour, it was on Wednesday when I was informed that there should be a temporary counsel assigned for the purposes of today's hearing. And then on Wednesday evening I was also informed that there is a decision that the lawyer appointed for the purposes of this hearing should also be permanently appointed for the appeals. I do not want to accept any experiment now because I already have a plan with Mr. Dershowitz to see how we can prepare the appeals brief. So I sent a letter to the gentleman in the Registry in which I said that if Mr. Dershowitz is unable to represent me, then I would like to defend myself. Of course for that purposes I would need the judgement translated into Serbian and the appropriate time to prepare the appeal. Then on Thursday evening I received notification that Mr. Dershowitz accepted and that made we very happy because it was within the deadline prescribed by the Tribunal. However, one hour later I was informed that there is an obstacle to the appointment of Mr. Dershowitz and the obstacle is that this particular rule now requires that he wants his brother as a co-counsel. I have to say that the counsel sitting here in front of me has very faithfully described the situation. I simply cannot [Realtime transcript read in error "I simply accept him"] accept him. It is not because I have anything against him. Indeed, this is the first time in my life that I see him. But this is a serious judgement, and I really have to find a plan, a serious plan, with which I am going to proceed in the appeals. And if you allow me just one more thing, maybe it was a mistake, but I received a notification from the Tribunal that the beginning of the 30-day deadline is going to be postponed until a permanent counsel is appointed. Now, the way I understood it it means that on the day that the counsel is appointed the 30-day deadline is going to start. So then I was really surprised last week when they told me that I have to solve this problem immediately, within several hours. So that is why I would like to ask you to enable me the only fair solution, and that is to appoint Mr. Dershowitz as my counsel and he should start with the appeals as soon as possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I thank you for this long explanation; however, I have to recall that as a matter of fact since the last decision signed by the President of this Tribunal, as a matter of fact you had ample time to reconcile this question. We are in an international tribunal, in a domestic setting this would be for about three days for -- to assign counsel. Of course you may be seated, Mr. Krajisnik. Please, sit down. Thank you, Madam Registrar. I was just made aware that on page 8, line 7, there was a mistake. You, Mr. Krajisnik, correctly as I recall said that you simply cannot accept Mr. Colin Nicholls, Queen's counsel, as counsel. This should please be corrected. Before giving the floor to the other party, let me give you some reflections on the problem before us. But let's please make a distinction between the question who can be assigned as co-counsel; is there a right to self-representation. And the second question, of course, the deadline or the deadlines. As regards the right to self-representation, we have ample jurisprudence in this Tribunal on self-representation before a Trial Chamber. There is, however -- anybody who knows something better please may correct me -- there's no jurisprudence at all about self-representation on appeal. As I mentioned at the beginning, this is an international tribunal applying a set of Rules of Procedure and Evidence being hybrid by nature and therefore please allow me a short view on domestic law. I think it's undisputed that in civil law countries and in particular in the -- in former Yugoslavia and in the states now on the territory of former Yugoslavia, when you have to hear a serious case, then it's mandatory to have counsel. Why? Simply because a person is not regarded able to overcome all these obstacles and legal hurdles in a criminal case of such a serious as the one we have before us. The approach in common law countries, as we all know, is different. There is of course the right of self-representation, it's enshrined in human rights tools like the international covenant, and this right to represent oneself is verbatim repeated in our Statute. However, we have to look into the jurisprudence, inter alia, of the US Supreme Court. The fundamental decision, no doubt, was Faretta versus California. And in Faretta versus California it was already said that if need may be, a judge even at a trial level may terminate self-representation under certain conditions. However, on appeal I think the leading case is Martinez versus Court of Appeal of California, Fourth Appellate District, where it reads in extreme clearness that they say that, "We the Judges are not aware of any historical consensus establishing a right of self-representation on appeal. In the appellate context, the balance between the two competing interests surely tips in favour of the state. The status of the accused defendant who retains a presumption of innocence throughout the trial process changes dramatically when a jury returns a guilty verdict. The requirement of representation by trained counsel implies no disrespect for the individual inasmuch as it tends to benefit the appellant as well as the court." According to this, we find, interestingly enough, in our -- in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of our twin court, the Arusha ad hoc tribunal dealing with genocide committed in 1994, Rule 45 quater, stating that, "The Chamber may, if it decides that in the interests of justice, instruct the Registrar to assign counsel to represent the interests of the accused." So therefore, I believe the decision to assign counsel was a reasonable one, and you had ample time in the past. In addition, we were informed -- may I ask the registrar if I'm wrong that first of all we were informed that Mr. Dershowitz was not able and willing to fill in the necessary forms for his representing an accused before this Tribunal; and second, that there was an obstacle because of his health condition, as referred to in his own letter as kidney-stones, being an obstacle to travel to The Hague. That as a matter of fact, it seems to be correct that there was not possible or no possibility to assign Mr. Dershowitz. And finally, it's in the discretion of the Registrar, as opposed to other legal systems, to assign the lead counsel, the lead counsel being a person in the 45 -- Rule 45 list, and I take it that immediately after the decision of the President you were given a list of these persons, as you yourself stated of counsel on the list under Rule 45. Then, this is concretised far more in Article 16(F), where it reads: "Member of the family or close friends of suspects, accused, and counsel are not eligible for assignment under the directive of counsel, expert, legal assistant, investigator, translator, or interpreter, unless the Registrar determines that the assignment is in the interests of justice." And I think, Mr. Nicholls, you referred to this situation prior to this referring to another case. However, it's under our system for the Registrar to exercise the discretion and until now I can't find any mistake in this exercise of discretion by the Registrar. But having said this I think we should hear now Prosecution on this question, limited to the question of assignment of counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: May it please the Court. I believe it would be premature at this point to determine whether or not Mr. Krajisnik can represent himself, and I do not know the circumstances under which Mr. Dershowitz's brother would or would not qualify under the Rule 16 that the Court has referred to. So we at this point take no position and would request that Mr. Nicholls be permitted to continue in his representation until there's some reason to believe there's a more suitable counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Having read all the documentation, in particular the history of the attempts to assign counsel, I think it's a matter of fairness, not only vis-a-vis Mr. Krajisnik, but also vis-a-vis other appellants waiting for a final judgement that indeed Mr. Nicholls who -- please don't misunderstand me, Mr. Krajisnik, is a highly -- is a counsel of high reputation, if I may say so, well-known from the famous Soering case with all due respect. And I think he's one of the best-placed counsel to sit in this court and hereby if there is no other motion brought by any of the parties, decide that it was correct the Registrar assigned Mr. Nicholls as counsel in this case, and this decision stands until further notice if there is no motion. And you will have time to file such a motion. This is so decided. However, the second question is a -- indeed, another valid point you raised and this is the notice of appeal. Until now we would not sit here because there is no appeal pending on the part of Mr. Krajisnik. There is only appeal from the Prosecution. However, fairness warrants that we think about the deadline in his former decision, of course always in the expectation that counsel would be assigned immediately, meaning within some days, that as of this date 30 days after this, notice of appeal has to be filed. I understand you referred already to one case, that within 30 days, having acted as Defence counsel myself, it's a mission impossible to present a proper notice of appeal even though, as I mentioned before, having once written the notice of appeal this is not the end of the story. Of course, you can go in further details later on, and you can even add reasons of appeal later on showing of good cause. This judgement we have before us handed down the 27th of September, 2006, is more than 400 pages long and the trial record corresponds to this. So therefore, we have to think about what is possible. I have to recall, once again referring to Article 16, that first in the interest -- Article 16(C): "In the interests of justice and at the request of lead counsel, the Registrar may assign a second counsel to assist with the defence of the suspect or accused." In this case the accused. "Furthermore, at the request of the lead counsel and where the interests of justice so require, the Registrar may assign co-counsel who does not speak either of the two working languages of the Tribunal but who speaks the native language of the suspect or accused. At the request of the lead counsel, the Registrar may assign other persons, such as legal assistants, consultants, investigators, and interpreters as required to provide support to counsel." So it is a matter for the now-acting lead counsel to take care to choose and I think it's necessary in this case, to choose a second counsel and the assistance in particular in interpreter always available to you that you can understand what Mr. Krajisnik wants to expresses in a language both of you understand. And as I've heard from the Registry, in the past this has happened already several times, and there is -- I think you also trust this person. There was the person acting not only as an interpreter but also as a person assisting all members of the team, and I take it that this person would be available for both of you. If I'm right, this person also enabled you to have a conversation this afternoon. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. So taking into account that of course immediately - and "immediately" means immediately and not as soon as possible - these persons you need have to be assigned, and it is for the lead counsel under the Rules, having consulted Mr. Krajisnik, to decide who should act in all these capacities, in particular it would be for you to decide whether, for example, Mr. Dershowitz, if he is able to travel again, could be one co-counsel. But this is for you. It's not -- it's neither for the Registry nor for the Bench to decide this. So all these possibilities are available for you. Taking this into account, and I think we shouldn't act here as being on an oriental bazaar, what would be from your point of view a reasonable time to file a notice of appeal?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that we should be given somewhere in the region of 60 days, in other words, twice what there would normally be available; or if not that, at least that Your Honour would allow an extension from the 15th of December or the equivalent of the 15th of December to the 8th of January, that's the court's recess period. If we consider at the present moment -- of course it may take me some time to organise a team. Ideally I would find somebody who's been previously involved; if not, there are of course very considerable difficulties. The record has to be circulated, it has to be read, and then we have to come together to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So it is a fairly elaborate process. So I would ask for, ideally, 60 days; if not 60 days, that Your Honour grants the extension that there would be if we were allowed the recess from the 15th of December to the 8th of January, that period of time as an extension. It's about the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I hear the Prosecution on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There is a slightly related issue in that Mr. Krajisnik's response brief is due on the 27th of December. My assumption is that Mr. Nicholls will represent him in the Prosecution's appeal, and we do not oppose an extension to file the notice of appeal but would like the Court to be aware that there were actually two filings that I believe Mr. Nicholls would be responsible for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You are referring to another case, Perisic?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, the Prosecution filed its notice of appeal on the 26th of October. Under the Rules our brief was then due on the 27th of November where we filed our brief. Sentencing appeals proceed on a more expeditious briefing schedule than appeals concerning convictions and sentences. By our calculation the response for the Defence brief is due the 27th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. Thank you for recalling, but I thought it goes without saying that filing the appeal brief by the Defence at the same time because no doubt you will deal with questions of sentencing also that at the same time the response will be due. You were kind enough to ask for this period of time by the end of court recess. However, I think it's a matter of judicial courtesy that we look back to previous cases, and there's the Blagojevic case. And when we take into account the additional time granted in this case, when counsel had changed from the trial phase to the appeals phase, taking this into account if you are moving for this I would be ready to grant an extension of time until the 5th of February that you can do this in due course; however, in a decent way and in a detailed way because it's not in the interests of justice that you file a notice of appeal and then later identify far more details and additional grounds of appeal and then we are seized of this. So please take it as an act of courtesy, but on the other time also in the interests of justice and in the interests of this Bench that over your request, if you so move, a deadline elapsing the 5th of February could be granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And that will be for the response as well as the notice of appeal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would there be any objection to this?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. So I take it that this was an oral motion on your part.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Rule 127 provides that there must be a motion, and this motion is hereby granted. The notice of appeal is due on 5th of February, 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have to, going now to the next point on the agenda, that's his pending -- THE APPELLANT: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As I said in the beginning it's only exceptionally that for personal reasons the floor is granted to an accused. In this system before this Tribunal under the Rules, I can give you the floor only on -- in extraordinary situations. And please, if you want to address the Court, do it by motion, assisted by your counsel. Thank you. THE APPELLANT: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything in English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises, she was on the wrong channel. The accused said: THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Does this mean I cannot be granted the floor now? Does this mean I cannot speak? Do I understand correctly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I have to answer your question in the affirmative. Being acquainted myself with a different system, however, our Rules of Procedure and Evidence are predominantly ones tailor-made in the Anglo-American system and I can't see any extraordinary circumstances why I should give you the floor right now. As I said if you so want it's always your right and you're always entitled to file a motion assisted by your counsel, and in addition I should not forget if there should be any health questions and if there should be any complaints on the United Nations Detention Unit's condition, please address me directly and I will not hesitate to convene another Status Conference. But these points on the agenda are decided for today. But there is still one matter and this is a matter of pending motions. In the Stanisic case, the Defence for Mr. Stanisic moved for a motion to get access to documents admitted into evidence in the trial case against Mr. Krajisnik. We have already heard Prosecution on this; however, because also documents tendered by the Defence and admitted as such are at stake, I think it's only fair to give also you the possibility to respond to this and if you have any objections that this material be transferred to the Stanisic case, then please do so, and taking into account the huge workload the Tribunal has. And I think it would be reasonable, being seized for the first time today with this problem, that there would be a deadline, say the 15th of February, ten days after this motion. Are there any obstacles from the side of the Prosecution because I take it that the case is not due to start in the near future?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. So decided. The 15th of February, please take note of these admissions in this matter and if you so want, respond. May I ask the parties, are there any other issues to be raised now?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is not the case. This concludes today's Status Conference. I thank you.
